text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Monday morning newspapers:
- Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek attends a two-day meeting of the United Nations General Council in New York, where he will also meet his Italian counterpart Romano Prodi.
- Drnovsek on Sunday visited the U.S. aircraft carrier John F. Kennedy, which entered the Slovenian port of Koper for the first time on Monday.
- Visits to Slovenia's coastal hotels over the weekend rose to 6,400, a seven percent increase from the same weekend last year. The number of foreign tourists rose by 17 percent.
- Some 7,000 singers from 249 choirs attended the 28th traditional meeting of choirs in Sentvid, some 30 km (18 miles) southeast from Ljubljana.
- A celebration marking the sixth anniversary of Slovenian independence will cost 15 million tolars ($95,663) this year, down from 60 million last year, authorities said.
- Almost 52 percent of Slovenians support the policies of Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek, 34 percent disagree with them, while the rest are undecided, an opinion poll by daily Dnevnik showed.
- Slovenian Iztok Cop, rowing gold medalist from the Mediterranean games, won the second race of the rowing World Cup in Paris on Sunday.
- The amount of cargo transferred through Slovenia's only port Luka Koper in May increased to 705,408 tones, a nine percent increase from May 1996, Luka said.
